opportunity: structsynth measures one function at a time and the layout ledger shares a struct_N only when one reader's claims are a SUBSET of the other's, so two functions that read overlapping-but-different parts of one record get a name each and each is declared to have only the fields its own function touched. On the eight layout builds 23 of the 77 ground-truth records kuna types at all are given more than one struct_N.
test_name: tests/stages/structmerge-siblings.xml (6 two-arm assertions: with `option structmerge off` each of two overlapping readers keeps its own record and re-deciding the first changes nothing; with `siblings` the second reader is answered by the union and re-deciding the first moves it onto the union) + unit tests (kuna_structmerge::tests: the option surface, the union of two overlapping readers with the first superseded, a contradicted claim at the same offset and one over the same bytes at a different offset, a single shared claim, the growth bound, the unclaimed-bytes veto, and off minting a record per reader)
binary: /tmp/layoutrecall-demo/two (gcc -O1, stripped; source in docs/features/structmerge/analysis.md) and the decbench full_run_address_2026-09-11 tree
inspiration: RecStruct (ASE 2021) section 4.2 merges the access patterns of every function that reaches one allocation site before deciding a layout; kuna had the per-function measurement and the program-wide ledger but no rule for combining two readers that merely overlap.

typesweep.note: type_match cannot see a record's members: a struct_2 * and a struct_3 * score the same. The option is metric-neutral by construction and the sweep confirms it.

hunks.the_one_respelling: grep -O2 sub_7110: the record gains a long member where it had undefined1 filler, so `v1 = a0->field_0x20` (an array member decaying to its address) becomes `v1 = &a0->field_0x20`, the same address with the pointer typed by the member

jobs: a --jobs N worker answers through the shard replay, which records the layout each request measured, so it never merges and a sharded run behaves as off -- the same divergence structsynth already has
